questions.q: The section **Cost per Accepted Task by Archetype** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.

Every budget account in the tree keeps budget = settled + reserved + free under atomic, logged transitions, so a delegation tree conserves spending and a stopped child keeps its reservation until its late bills settle.
A one-time adaptation investment recovers its cost after N* = C_adapt / (C_base - C_adapted) tasks, never if the per-task saving is nonpositive, and only while acceptance stays equal.

Accepted tasks per unit time is the platform's deliverable, so sustaining goodput G at acceptance alpha requires admitting G/alpha trajectories and any change that lowers acceptance raises offered load.
